standing_checks.description: Every closed trade must have pos.origin read and reported. A trade whose origin is not the live selection path (daily.py queueing into main, pooled or capped) is named in the handoff and its P and L stated separately from the bucket total, never folded into it. Batch 20260910: GMMPFAUDLR (pbook cohort2) and SAHYADRI (cohort3) sat inside main's Rs 5,048.17 worth minus Rs 3,488.83 between them, n=2 of 7 main paths, marked only by a column no report reads. Checkable per trade because origin is a stored column with a value on every row.

Every closed trade's fill_source must be exactly one of confirmed, corpus:open, reconciled, live:<feed>, or paper:etf_trend for the fund strategy. Any other value is reported as an anomaly and the entry price verified against that day's corpus open before the trade is categorised. Batch 20260910: HAPPYFORGE main id 3 reads corpus:open (backfilled) from an out-of-band UPDATE, n=1 of 11 records. Three further rows carry annotated variants and are still OPEN (ids 14 and 15 pooled, id 23 capped), so this recurs in a future batch by arithmetic. Checkable per trade by string equality against the set positions.py actually writes.

Every closed trade with exit_reason=time must have bars_held equal to selection.HOLD_DAYS exactly. Where it does not, compute the signed displacement against the close of the bar the rule named, in percentage points and in rupees, and report the sign explicitly. A favourable displacement is categorised as Process Deviation exactly as an unfavourable one is. Batch 20260910: YUKEN main id 1 held 12 bars and exited at plus 12.31 percent against plus 7.47 percent on its own bar 10, Rs 2,221 of the Rs 5,479.80 outage-attributable and FAVOURABLE, n=1 of 5 time exits. Checkable per trade from bars_held and exit_reason on the row, with no need to know which sessions the scheduler missed.

Any trade with origin != breakout is reported in non_strategy_positions and excluded from the error profile. Checkable on one row: does it carry an origin field, and if it is not breakout, is it in the separate section with no category?

Every filled trade records whether its fill open sat at or near the upper circuit band (within 0.05 points of the exchange limit for that name). Checkable on one row: compare the fill open against the signal close and the band. This accumulates the data a band-relative rule shape would need, without proposing one.

definitions_used.bars_held: positions.bars_held(entry_day, exit_day) -- trading bars STRICTLY AFTER the entry day through the exit day. This is the clock the exit rule itself runs on (positions.step: `held >= HOLD_DAYS`), so time_exit_mismatch is measured against it. definitions_used.pnl_pct: (exit_price - entry_price) / entry_price * 100, gross of charges. The rupee figures (net_rupees_by_bucket, per_cluster.pnl) are NET of charges and modelled impact.

verifications.item: the Rs 45,000 per-stock question -- RESOLVED FROM THE SIZING CODE, NOT A DEVIATION
verifications.verdict: expected next-open drift. No flag. No vocabulary entry covers it and none is needed.
verifications.evidence: selection.build (strategies/breakout/selection.py) sets `ref = s.close[i]` -- the SIGNAL close -- and calls position_size(capital, ref). position_size caps at `cap_value = capital * DEPLOY_PCT / 100 / max_pos` and takes qty = int(cap_value/ref). positions.queue() stores that qty; positions.step(), fill_live() and mark_open() all set entry_px WITHOUT touching qty (mark_open changes qty only when a caller passes one, and no caller does). So quantity is fixed at the signal close and the fill lands at the next open. Reproduced: position_size(equity_at_queue, signal_close) returns the recorded qty on 11 of 11 rows, exactly. And ORDER VALUE AT THE SIGNAL CLOSE IS UNDER THE CAP ON 11 OF 11 -- the largest is NATCAPSUQ pooled at 44,973.60 of 45,000.00. Every overshoot at the fill equals that row's fill premium to two decimals: ARCHIDPLY 46,250.50 vs 44,269.47 = +4.47% = its fill_premium_pct 4.47; YUKEN 45,900.00 vs 44,979.45 = +2.05% = 2.05; SOMANYCERA +1.17 = 1.17; NATCAPSUQ pooled +0.50 = 0.50; WELENT pooled +0.15 = 0.15. Sizing never saw the fill price.
verifications.correction_to_the_orchestrator: The ceiling is NOT a fixed Rs 45,000. daily.py:86 calls selection.build(corpus, day, capital=bs['equity']) and positions.summary() returns equity = CAPITAL + that bucket's REALISED P&L, so the cap is equity * 75% / 5 and moves with realised results. main's cap was 44,307.05 when ARCHIDPLY and WELENT/main were sized and 43,589.12 for NATCAPSUQ/main, because main was carrying realised losses. Measured against the cap that actually applied, ARCHIDPLY's overshoot is +4.4% rather than the +2.8% the orchestrator computed against a flat 45,000 -- and it is still not a breach, because the rule can only bind at the signal close.

temporal_concentration_flags.flag: temporally concentrated -- may reflect a regime, not a rule
temporal_concentration_flags.reading: By the LETTER of the rule -- share of occurrences in the last 25% of the exit-date lookback (2026-09-06..09-10) -- this is 0 of 2 and would NOT flag. By substance it is 2 of 2 inside a single 3-day window that is 3 of the 18 calendar days the batch spans. I flag it on substance. The non-equity case is why: 36.4% of fund trades sitting in one recent window made a precious-metals rally look like the strategy working, and suppressing a 100% concentration on a definitional technicality is the same error with better paperwork.
temporal_concentration_flags.but: It is concentrated BY CONSTRUCTION -- the outage_window flag IS the date range -- and the driver is an infrastructure event (L91 WAL outage, reverted; data/known_gaps.json records 2026-09-03 as a full-session capture gap), not a market regime and not a rule. A closed 3-day event. The flag is raised so that a SECOND cluster in a different window is visible as new rather than as more of the same.
